MK-CF-M-030.label: Each person’s pay
MK-CF-M-030.answers: What everyone in the household earns before anything is taken out.
MK-CF-M-030.formula: gross a year = the sum of every earner’s wage, each annualised from the rhythm they are paid in
inputs: MK-CF-I-002 how often it is paid
decisions: A wage entered for a rhythm is annualised by that rhythm, never by a flat twelve.

MK-CF-M-031.label: Take-home
MK-CF-M-031.answers: What actually reaches the bank each month, after federal tax and 401(k) — for one earner, and for the household.
MK-CF-M-031.formula: for one earner: what they entered, or their gross less federal tax less their own 401(k). For the household: the sum of the earners’ figures, never a second calculation.
decisions: Federal income tax only when it is calculated — no Social Security, Medicare or state tax (MK-CF-D-001).
MK-CF-M-031.refusal: Shows $0 until a wage is entered.
MK-CF-M-031.note: ONE figure over two sets: one earner, and the household — so a total and its parts cannot disagree (rule 2). It wears ≈ whenever the figure was calculated rather than entered.

MK-CF-M-035.answers: By roughly how much the calculated take-home overstates what will reach the bank, because only federal income tax is taken out of it.
MK-CF-M-035.formula: overstated by = Σ over earners of (Social Security 6.2% of the wage up to the wage base + Medicare 1.45% of the whole wage + 0.9% of the wage above the additional-tax threshold) ÷ 12

MK-CF-M-037.label: Take-home each month
MK-CF-M-037.answers: What reaches the bank in a usual month, from every source of income added together.
MK-CF-M-037.formula: take-home a usual month = Σ of every source’s take-home in a usual month; a source that lands in one month of the year is not spread across twelve
decisions: A once-a-year source keeps its own month and is shown separately, never averaged in.
MK-CF-M-037.refusal: Shows $0 on a fresh account, with the door to enter income — never a dash.
MK-CF-M-037.note: FOUND BY THE WORKED EXAMPLE AND FIXED THE SAME DAY, 2026-09-28. This total read $9,798/month while the two take-home lines beneath it (MK-CF-M-038) added to $9,398 — $400 apart, exactly the spouse's monthly 401(k). MK-CF-F-060 salaryGrossByMonth sums EVERY earner's wage (his ruling, 2026-08-27) but the 401(k) taken off that household gross was written as the first earner's alone, so a spouse's was never subtracted — the take-home read too high by their contribution, and the taxable base too. NOT A NEW QUESTION: he ruled this on 2026-09-12 on income-end-to-end v07 — "one card disagreeing with itself; corrected to the take-home line" — and the correction reached the mock and not the code. Now MK-CF-F-206 householdK401ByMonth counts every earner in the months that earner is paid, and src/__tests__/guard_total_agrees_with_its_lines.test.ts holds the ruling. The six personas all passed throughout because none had a spouse with their own wage AND their own 401(k); twoEarnersBoth401k now does.

MK-XS-M-004.formula: wealth generated ÷ the money that was working in the window, counting each contribution for the part of the window it was there; over a window longer than a year it is shown as a yearly rate
inputs: MK-XS-I-020 the records of money movements
decisions: ONE MEANING OF RETURN (B-97, 2026-09-25): dividends and interest are in it, because "Wealth generated" beside it counts them.
A RATE NEEDS SOMETHING TO STAND ON: with no beginning read from the record and no movement to point at, it shows nothing rather than a confident +0.00%.
IT REFUSES WHEN TIMING WOULD DRIVE IT: where money moved in or out in amounts large enough that WHEN it moved decides the percentage, the screen shows the dollar walk instead.
OVER A YEAR IT IS A YEARLY RATE and the screen says so (his ruling, 2026-08-18, restated 2026-09-25).
MK-XS-M-004.refusal: Nothing is shown, and the walk beneath says in words why — either the record cannot reach the beginning, or money moved in amounts that would decide the percentage.

worked.given: An account worth $30,000 on 31 Dec 2025 (100 VTI at $260 plus $4,000 cash) and $32,000 on 28 Sep 2026, with nothing paid in or taken out and $825 of it arriving as dividends.

MK-XS-M-004.note: DECLARED 2026-09-30. It is the screen’s headline figure — the number in the summary band, on every window chip, and on Home’s glance card — and NO DOOR DECLARED IT. The old metric register has carried the identifier since the start ("▲ up/▼ down $X (Y%) this month · Return · YOUR RETURN"), but the code declared the ending value, the wealth generated and the walk and not the percentage a person actually reads. That is why Home could print a return of its own and no gate noticed (B-112): there was no figure for the two screens to disagree about. It is an MK-XS identifier because it is on more than one screen.

MK-PF-M-001.label: Ending value
MK-PF-M-001.answers: What your investments are worth at the end of the window you picked.
MK-PF-M-001.formula: the sum of every investment account’s value today

worked.given: An account worth $30,000 on 31 Dec 2025 (100 VTI at $260 plus $4,000 cash) and $46,600 on 28 Sep 2026, with $6,000 paid in on 1 Apr and $825 of dividends received.

MK-PF-M-002.label: Wealth generated
MK-PF-M-002.answers: What the money itself made in the window — not what you added to it.
MK-PF-M-002.formula: ending − beginning − what you put in + what you took out
decisions: ONE MEANING OF RETURN (B-97, 2026-09-25): dividends and interest are part of this, so the return beside it counts them too.
MK-PF-M-002.refusal: The record cannot reach the start of this window, so there is nothing honest to subtract from.

worked.given: An account worth $30,000 on 31 Dec 2025 (100 VTI at $260 plus $4,000 cash) and $46,600 on 28 Sep 2026, with $6,000 paid in on 1 Apr and $825 of dividends received.

MK-PF-M-003.label: HOW $X BECAME $Y · ALL ACCOUNTS
MK-PF-M-003.answers: Every line that took the beginning to the ending, so it can be checked by eye.
MK-PF-M-003.formula: beginning + contributions − withdrawals + wealth generated = ending, by construction
decisions: Whatever the records cannot explain lands in the change-in-value line rather than being silently dropped.

worked.given: An account worth $30,000 on 31 Dec 2025 (100 VTI at $260 plus $4,000 cash) and $46,600 on 28 Sep 2026, with $6,000 paid in on 1 Apr and $825 of dividends received.

MK-PF-M-004.label: Ending market value (per account)
MK-PF-M-004.answers: What one account is worth at the end of the window.
MK-PF-M-004.formula: the sum of that account’s holdings, at today’s prices, plus its cash

worked.given: An account worth $30,000 on 31 Dec 2025 (100 VTI at $260 plus $4,000 cash) and $46,600 on 28 Sep 2026, with $6,000 paid in on 1 Apr and $825 of dividends received. Asked of that one account.

MK-PF-M-005.label: each account and its ending value
MK-PF-M-005.answers: One line per account, and what it is worth — the parts that sum to the whole above.
MK-PF-M-005.formula: each investment account’s value, named by the account
decisions: Named by ACCOUNT, not by institution — two accounts at one broker must be tellable apart (founder screenshot, 2026-08-17).
MK-PF-M-005.refusal: One account only — the whole walk above already says it.

worked.given: An account worth $30,000 on 31 Dec 2025 (100 VTI at $260 plus $4,000 cash) and $46,600 on 28 Sep 2026, with $6,000 paid in on 1 Apr and $825 of dividends received. Each account is asked separately, from the same door as the total.

MK-PF-M-010.label: Left in <fund> it became $X (up/down $Y, Z%)
MK-PF-M-010.answers: What your money actually did, where it actually was.
MK-PF-M-010.formula: the amount × (the fund’s price today ÷ its price at the start of the window)
decisions: Price changes only — dividends are not in it, and the screen says so.
MK-PF-M-010.refusal: No price history over the whole window — the screen shows nothing rather than a shortened one.

worked.given: $10,000 left in BND for 12 months, against moving it to VTI. BND closed $72.00 a year ago and $73.80 now; VTI closed $250.00 and $290.00.

MK-PF-M-011.label: Moved to <fund> it would be $X
MK-PF-M-011.answers: What the same money would have become in the other fund.
MK-PF-M-011.formula: the amount × (the other fund’s price today ÷ its price at the start of the window)
decisions: A road not taken, priced from real history — never a projection forward.
MK-PF-M-011.refusal: No price history for the other fund over the whole window.

worked.given: $10,000 left in BND for 12 months, against moving it to VTI. BND closed $72.00 a year ago and $73.80 now; VTI closed $250.00 and $290.00.

MK-PF-M-012.label: Difference: $X more/less if you had moved
MK-PF-M-012.answers: What the move would have been worth, in money.
MK-PF-M-012.formula: what it would have become, less what it did become
MK-PF-M-012.refusal: Either fund missing its history means no difference is stated.

worked.given: $10,000 left in BND for 12 months, against moving it to VTI. BND closed $72.00 a year ago and $73.80 now; VTI closed $250.00 and $290.00.

MK-MN-M-003.label: $X left / up to $Y
MK-MN-M-003.answers: How much more you can still put into this account this year.
MK-MN-M-003.formula: the IRS limit for your age this year, less what has gone in already
inputs: MK-XS-I-030 tax filing status and age
decisions: The age tested is the age ATTAINED IN THE YEAR (his ruling G1) — someone turning 50 in December gets the catch-up for the whole year.
MK-MN-M-003.refusal: No birth year entered — the catch-up cannot be judged, so the limit says it is the base one.

worked.given: Born 1965 — so 61 during 2026. Paying in $1,200/month to a 401(k), $300 to a Roth IRA and $150 to an HSA; not on Medicare. Read in September, so four months of the year are left.

MK-MN-M-004.label: about $X of the $Y limit
MK-MN-M-004.answers: What has gone in so far, against what the law allows.
MK-MN-M-004.formula: what you entered per month × 12, capped at the limit
decisions: Capped at the limit: a figure above it would be describing a contribution the law does not permit.

worked.given: Born 1965 — so 61 during 2026. Paying in $1,200/month to a 401(k), $300 to a Roth IRA and $150 to an HSA; not on Medicare. Read in September, so four months of the year are left.

MK-MN-M-005.label: about $X for the rest of the year
MK-MN-M-005.answers: What filling the remaining room would cost you each month.
MK-MN-M-005.formula: what is left ÷ the months remaining, this month included
decisions: THIS MONTH COUNTS (his ruling G36). Leaving it out told people to save more per month than they need to.

worked.given: Born 1965 — so 61 during 2026. Paying in $1,200/month to a 401(k), $300 to a Roth IRA and $150 to an HSA; not on Medicare. Read in September, so four months of the year are left.

MK-MN-M-029.label: each contribution and its amount
MK-MN-M-029.answers: One line per tax-advantaged account, and what has gone into it.
MK-MN-M-029.formula: the monthly amount you entered for that account × 12
decisions: Enrolled in Medicare means NO HSA contribution is allowed at all — not a smaller one (his ruling G10, 2026-09-08).

worked.given: Born 1965 — so 61 during 2026. Paying in $1,200/month to a 401(k), $300 to a Roth IRA and $150 to an HSA; not on Medicare. Read in September, so four months of the year are left.

MK-MN-M-006.label: $X of $Y used — the line marks 30%
MK-MN-M-006.answers: How much of your available credit you are using.
MK-MN-M-006.formula: what is owed on your cards ÷ the total limit across them
decisions: Under 30% is the mark the line shows, because that is the level credit scoring treats as unstretched.
MK-MN-M-006.refusal: No limit entered — there is no ratio, and a 0% would read as "you have used none of it".

worked.given: $3,100 owed on the cards against $12,000 of total limit — 25.8% of the line in use.

MK-MN-M-027.label: each taxable line and its amount
MK-MN-M-027.answers: One line per kind of income the year is taxed on, and what it came to.
MK-MN-M-027.formula: wages, self-employment, rent, interest and dividends, and benefits — each from what you entered or what your accounts recorded
decisions: Interest and dividends come from the RECORDS where they exist, not from an estimate — an estimate on a tax page reads as a figure to file.
MK-MN-M-027.refusal: A line with nothing behind it does not appear at all.

worked.given: Filing jointly for 2026 on $169,200 of wages, with $19,200 paid into 401(k)s between the two of them and the $32,200 standard deduction.

MK-MN-M-028.label: Gross income · 401(k) contribution · Standard deduction · Taxable income · Non-taxable
MK-MN-M-028.answers: The walk from what you earned to what you are taxed on, in the order the form takes it.
MK-MN-M-028.formula: gross, less the 401(k), less the standard deduction for your filing status = taxable income
inputs: MK-XS-I-030 tax filing status and age
decisions: ONE tax function across the app (rule 2) — the same one that sets the band on your pay.

worked.given: Filing jointly for 2026 on $169,200 of wages, with $19,200 paid into 401(k)s between the two of them and the $32,200 standard deduction.

MK-CF-M-012.label: RECEIVED · <month> — each payment
MK-CF-M-012.answers: Each payment that has actually arrived this month, and when.
MK-CF-M-012.formula: the income records dated inside the month

MK-CF-M-016.label: BIG-TICKET RADAR — <bill> · due <month>
MK-CF-M-016.answers: A bill big enough to plan for, and the month it falls in.
MK-CF-M-016.formula: the dated bills above the everyday size, in date order
decisions: A regular monthly debt is never a radar item: a warning you see every month stops being a warning.
MK-CF-M-016.refusal: Nothing unusual ahead — the section keeps its heading and says so.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

MK-CF-M-017.label: well above your usual <category>
MK-CF-M-017.answers: Why this one expense stood out.
MK-CF-M-017.formula: this expense against the typical one in its category, over the months logged
decisions: There must BE a usual to compare against: with too little logged, nothing is flagged. A first month’s expenses are not unusual, they are all there is.
MK-CF-M-017.refusal: Too little history to call anything unusual.

MK-CF-M-026.label: the months a paycheck lands
MK-CF-M-026.answers: Which months carry an extra paycheck, for anyone paid fortnightly.
MK-CF-M-026.formula: the pay dates that fall in each month, counted
MK-CF-M-026.refusal: Paid monthly — every month carries one, so there is nothing to point out.

MK-CF-M-028.label: each bill and the day it falls
MK-CF-M-028.answers: One line per bill ahead, with its date and what is left after it.
MK-CF-M-028.formula: each dated bill in the window, in date order, with the running balance after it
decisions: A bill with NO date is not on the calendar — a date nobody gave would be read as one they did. It is still counted in the month’s total.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

MK-MN-M-030.label: $X left <account> on <date>
MK-MN-M-030.answers: What would be left after each bill, so a shortfall is visible before it happens.
MK-MN-M-030.formula: the balance you start with, less each bill as its date passes

MK-CF-M-001.label: Expenses
MK-CF-M-001.answers: What you plan to spend in a month, as one line on the flow.
MK-CF-M-001.formula: your budget — the per-category plan added up
decisions: One line on This month, and the Expenses tab is its detail — not a second answer to the same question (his correction, 2026-09-28).
MK-CF-M-001.refusal: No budget set — the line reads "not set" and offers the door, never a planned surplus built on a guess.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

MK-CF-M-002.label: = Planned surplus
MK-CF-M-002.answers: What is left over in the month if everything goes to plan.
MK-CF-M-002.formula: the inflow, less every debt payment due, less the budget, less each big-ticket item
decisions: EVERY ROW SHOWN IS A ROW DEDUCTED (his rule under the approved design): nothing appears on This month without being in the sum.
MK-CF-M-002.refusal: No budget set — there is no planned surplus, and the screen says so rather than guessing one.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

MK-CF-M-003.label: = Actual surplus so far
MK-CF-M-003.answers: What is actually left, on what has really happened so far this month.
MK-CF-M-003.formula: the inflow received, less each debt actually paid, less everything logged by hand and imported
decisions: An unpaid debt shows $0 with its due date — never silently dropped, or the surplus would flatter the month.
A card payment is counted ONCE: connected card → the imported purchases are the expense and the payment is a radar note; not connected → the payment IS the expense.
MK-CF-M-003.refusal: Nothing logged and no card linked — it says so and offers the door.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

MK-CF-M-004.label: each row of the month — what it is and what it costs
MK-CF-M-004.answers: One line per thing in or out this month, so the surplus can be checked by reading down the column.
MK-CF-M-004.formula: the inflow; each debt by name; the budget; each big-ticket item — each with its own amount
decisions: Drawn from the approved design (cash-flow_v01): the flow is SPELLED OUT, not summarised into three numbers.
MK-CF-M-004.refusal: A section with nothing in it keeps its heading and says so.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.
